What is the best hair colour management software for UK salons?

There are four serious options in the UK: Vish, SalonScale, Color Bar Manager and Daviana ColorLab. They all weigh or track the colour you mix and show what it cost. The best one for you depends mostly on your booking system. Vish plugs into systems such as Phorest and SalonIQ, SalonScale connects directly to Square, Color Bar Manager can start without a scale, and ColorLab shares one record with the Daviana diary and till.

26 September 2026·6 min read

The short answer

  • Hair colour management software weighs each bowl, saves the formula to the client and shows what the colour cost, so you can stop overmixing and charge for what was used.
  • The first question is not features but fit: which booking system you are keeping, and whether the colour charge will reach the client's bill without retyping.
  • Three of the four publish prices in US dollars only. Convert them, add VAT, and add scales and tablets before you compare with a UK price.
  • Plan for adoption. Software that needs every bowl weighed only pays if the team weighs every bowl.
  • Work out what a head of colour costs you today before you buy anything. That is the number the software is meant to reduce.

Most salons know their colour bill and almost none know what a single head of colour costs them. Colour gets mixed by eye, the leftover goes down the sink, and the product used on a long root and lengths never quite makes it onto the bill. Hair colour management software exists to close that gap.

This guide compares the four tools UK salon owners are most likely to be looking at. The competitor facts come from each company's own pricing and product pages, checked on 26 September 2026 and listed at the end. We make one of the four, ColorLab, so we have said plainly where each of the others is the better choice.

What does hair colour management software actually do?

At the colour bar, the stylist opens the client, picks the shades and pours onto a connected scale. The software records the grams of each product and developer, saves that formula to the client, and works out what the bowl cost from your product prices. Most tools then add three things on top:

  • Formula history, so the next visit starts from exactly what was used last time, whoever is on the chair.
  • Charging, so colour used beyond what the service includes can be added to the bill.
  • Stock, so reordering follows what was really poured rather than a guess.

The saving comes from two places: less colour mixed and thrown away, and fewer services where the colour used was never charged. There is more on where that money goes in how much hair colour is your salon really wasting?

Which one fits your salon?

Start from the booking system you are keeping, then from how your team works.

  • You are staying on Phorest, SalonIQ, Shortcuts or Zenoti. Vish lists integrations with all of them, and a paid Sync+ add-on for Phorest salons. It is the most established choice for a salon that is not changing its diary. See our ColorLab vs Vish comparison.
  • You take payments on Square. SalonScale integrates with Square directly, publishes simple per-stylist-band pricing, and lets you use a scale you already own.
  • You want to start without changing habits on day one. Color Bar Manager is built to be useful before every stylist weighs every bowl, starts at $15 a week, and has a 30-day money-back guarantee.
  • You want colour on the same record as your diary and till. Daviana ColorLab reads the day's colour clients and per-stylist prices from the Daviana diary and, where a salon turns it on, posts the colour charge back to the appointment. There is no sync to keep in step, the price is in pounds with VAT included, and a formula can start from a photo of the hair.

If none of those describes you, the tie-breaker is usually the one your team will actually use at 4pm on a Saturday.

What should you check before you buy?

  • The real monthly price in pounds. Three of the four publish US dollar prices. Convert, add VAT where it applies, and add scales, tablets and any setup fee.
  • Whether the charge reaches the bill. Weighing without charging only saves the overmix. Ask exactly how the extra colour gets onto the client's bill in your booking system, and whether anyone has to retype it.
  • Your colour brands. Check the shade library covers the lines you use, including any own-label colour.
  • What happens to formulas if you leave. Your clients' colour history is the most valuable data in the salon. Ask how you would export it.
  • How the team will use it. A scale by every mixing station and a two-minute routine matter more than any feature on the list.

How much could it save your salon? A worked example

Take two figures from your own records: what you spend on professional colour in a month, and how many colour services you do. Say it is £2,000 across 250 services, which is £8 a service on average. If weighing shows that one bowl in ten is overmixed by a quarter, that is roughly £50 a month of colour in the sink. If one service in twenty uses more colour than the price includes and it never reaches the bill, add those services at your extra-colour charge.

These are example figures, not industry averages. Replace them with yours in our free salon colour cost calculator, which works from your own spend and does not ask for an email. If the answer is less than the software costs, you do not need it yet.

Questions salon owners ask

Do I need a special scale for colour management software?

It depends on the tool. Vish sells its own scales at $195 each and needs a tablet per scale. SalonScale lets you use a scale you already have and includes a free precision scale with annual billing. Color Bar Manager does not need a scale to start. Daviana ColorLab uses a Bluetooth precision scale that guides each pour to the gram.

Which hair colour management software is cheapest?

On published prices, Color Bar Manager starts lowest at $15 a week or $47 a month, and Vish Solo is $40 a month for a single stylist before scales and setup. For a team, compare the plan for your number of stylists plus hardware, converted to pounds with VAT, against Daviana ColorLab at £80 a month including VAT.

Does colour management software work with Phorest?

Vish lists Phorest among its integrations and offers a paid Sync+ add-on for Phorest salons. SalonScale integrates directly with Square only. Color Bar Manager says it works alongside existing salon software. Daviana ColorLab is part of Daviana rather than an add-on to Phorest.

Can I charge clients for the extra colour they use?

That is one of the main reasons to weigh. Vish sends exact usage and prices to the front desk, SalonScale connects to Square at checkout, and Daviana ColorLab can post the colour charge back to the appointment. Whichever you use, put your extra-colour policy on your price list so clients are not surprised.

Is colour management software worth it for a solo stylist?

Sometimes. A solo stylist knows their own habits, so the saving is smaller than in a team. Run your own figures through a colour cost calculator first; if the monthly saving is less than the subscription, a notebook and a kitchen scale will do for now.
